sentences.text: If you drive the same strip of dirt every day, you have a road.
But rain turns the dirt to mud, and the car gets stuck.
So you dig out the mud and pack in crushed stone.
But now rain soaks into the stone and sits there.
So you lay a pipe with holes under it to carry water away.
But now cars kick up loose stones and dust.
So you seal the top with asphalt, which locks the stone in.
This is a paved road, built in layers.
Asphalt is about 95 percent stone, sand and gravel by weight.
Add a center line, a stop line and a street sign.
Congratulations, you have built a road.
